description: Techniques adversaries use to gain an initial foothold within a network, such as phishing emails with malicious attachments, exploiting public-facing applications, or using valid credentials obtained through prior compromise.
Techniques that result in adversary-controlled code running on a local or remote system, including command-line interpreters, scripting engines, and scheduled tasks.
Techniques adversaries use to maintain access to systems across restarts, credential changes, and other interruptions, such as creating new accounts or modifying startup processes.
Techniques adversaries use to gain higher-level permissions on a system or network, often by exploiting misconfigurations or vulnerabilities in access control mechanisms.
Techniques adversaries use to avoid detection, including disabling security software, obfuscating malicious code, or clearing logs of their activity.
Techniques for stealing credentials such as account names and passwords, including keylogging, credential dumping, and brute-force attacks.
Techniques adversaries use to gain knowledge about a system and internal network, such as enumerating accounts, network shares, and installed software.
Techniques adversaries use to move through a network from one system to another, often using stolen credentials or remote services.
Techniques adversaries use to gather data of interest prior to exfiltration, such as capturing screenshots, keystrokes, or accessing local files.
Techniques adversaries use to steal data from a network, including transferring it over command-and-control channels or physical media.
